title: Cab Driver Earnings Per Hour After Fuel Cost
excerpt: Learn a simple daily method to track what you keep after fuel, charging, servicing and empty kilometres.
body: Cab driver earnings per hour should mean what you keep after fuel and running costs, not only the fare total in the app. This guide shows a simple way to check your hour, kilometre, fuel and dead-kilometre numbers every day.
## Start with your app numbers, then subtract costs

Uber Help says you can track earnings by week, day or trip in the Driver app through the fare icon or the Earnings tab. It also says Trip History shows recent trips, and choosing one trip shows gross fare and net fare. Use these numbers as your starting point, not as your final take-home amount.

At the end of each shift, note four things in a notebook or phone note. Write the hours you were online, the earnings shown for the day, the total kilometres on your odometer, and the money spent on fuel or charging. If you work on more than one app, write separate trip totals if the app shows them, but keep one total for fuel and kilometres.

To find your earnings per hour, divide the money left after fuel or charging by the hours you worked. To find your earning per kilometre, divide the same money left by total kilometres driven, not only paid trip kilometres. This makes short waiting time, long pickup distance and empty return trips visible.

Uber’s Driver Dashboard also shows earnings, according to Uber Help. Check it when your phone screen is too small for a proper review. Do this once a week so you can compare Monday to Sunday, instead of judging your whole work by one good or bad day.
## Compare petrol, CNG and EV cost per kilometre

Fuel choice changes the money left in your pocket. TOI Auto compared running costs on September 28, 2026, using example prices and efficiency figures. It estimated a home-charged EV at about Rs 1.14 per km, CNG at about Rs 2.62 per km, and petrol at about Rs 7.41 per km, with the article clearly saying these are fuel or electricity costs only, not total ownership costs.

The same TOI Auto report used Mumbai examples, including CNG at Rs 88 per kg and petrol at Rs 111.21 per litre. It also said a public fast-charging example at Rs 20 per kWh could take the EV energy cost to about Rs 2.86 per km before charging losses and other charges. This is why an EV is strongest when your charging is cheap and easy, while CNG is useful when pumps are near your work area and queues are manageable.

Use this method for your own car instead of copying any one city’s number. Fill CNG or petrol fully, reset the trip meter, and note kilometres before the next fill. For an EV, note units charged and kilometres driven. After three to five shifts, divide the fuel or electricity money by kilometres driven. That is your real energy cost per km.
## Save fuel with daily driving and maintenance habits

Small driving habits matter because cab work has many starts, stops and U-turns. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs Drivers Handbook says correct tyre pressure should be maintained because under-inflation reduces fuel efficiency and over-inflation damages tyres. It also advises switching off the engine when a stop is expected to be more than 2 minutes, and not riding the clutch.

Make these checks part of your first 10 minutes. Check tyre pressure when tyres are cold, look for uneven tyre wear, and listen for brake drag or engine roughness. Keep the AC filter and engine air filter clean as per the car maker’s service schedule, because a hard-working city cab spends many hours in dust and traffic.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways road safety book says running with one tyre under-inflated by 8 psi can reduce tyre life by 15,000 km and increase fuel consumption by 4 percent. It also says a poorly maintained vehicle can increase fuel consumption by up to 15 percent. For a driver doing high daily kilometres, these are not small numbers.

Do servicing on time and keep bills or service records. Use the oil grade recommended for the car and avoid delaying small repairs that affect mileage, such as spark plugs, filters, wheel alignment, brake binding or CNG tuning. The aim is simple: the car should use less fuel for the same trip distance.
## Cut dead kilometres before and after trips

Dead kilometres are kilometres driven without a paying rider. They include going far for pickup, returning empty from a low-demand area, driving around while waiting, and going home without a rider. These kilometres reduce both earnings per hour and earnings per kilometre.

Uber says its destination feature lets you set a destination so the app can find riders travelling in the same direction. If this feature is available in your city and app, use it when you are going home, going to a CNG pump, moving towards a busy area or ending your shift. Do not use extra kilometres chasing every possible hotspot if your fuel cost is already high.

Uber also describes back-to-back trips, where the app can send the next trip while you are completing the current one. When your app offers this, it can reduce waiting time between trips. Still, check pickup distance, traffic and fuel situation before accepting any trip, because a long unpaid pickup can spoil a good fare.

End every day with one question: did the car move mainly with riders, or mainly empty? If empty kilometres were high, change your start point, fuel stop, lunch break area or end-of-day route the next day. title: Uber Airport Queue Guide for Indian Cab Drivers
excerpt: Learn how airport pickups, waiting areas and queue checks can help you decide when an airport trip is worth your time.
body: If you search for uber airport queue, the main thing to know is simple. Airport trips can be good, but only when you understand the waiting area, pickup zone, flight demand and the time you may lose compared with city trips.
## How airport pickups are different from normal city trips

Uber’s driver guide says an airport trip appears in the Driver app like a normal trip, but the airport may require you to wait in a designated area before you receive a request. The app then shows the approved pickup or dropoff point for that airport.

This matters because airport pickup points are not always at the normal arrivals gate. Uber says airports may have special zones for Uber and other rideshare services, and the Driver app guides you to the designated pickup location.

For dropoffs, Uber advises drivers to ask the rider whether the flight is domestic or international and which airline they are using. This helps you follow the terminal signs and avoid circling inside the airport road system.

Airport surcharges, where applicable, are included in the price riders see when they request a trip to or from an airport, according to Uber’s driver page. Uber says those charges are paid to the airport by Uber, so you should not treat them as a separate cash discussion with the rider.
## How the airport queue works in the app

Uber Help describes the Virtual Queue as a system that organises airport requests by order of arrival in the designated airport area. In that model, your place depends on when you entered the queue area, not on whether you are parked closest to the passenger.

You should join only from the waiting area shown in the Driver app. Uber Help says staying outside the designated area can prevent you from receiving airport requests, and going offline or leaving the area may make you lose your place.

If you wait too long, first check whether you are in the correct waiting area. Uber Help says long airport waits can happen when there are fewer flights landing, at certain times of day, or because of weather conditions.

Uber Help gives two useful warning signs for drivers: waiting longer than 2 hours for UberX or UberXL, or longer than 2.5 hours for Exec. It also says Airport Rematch or Priority Queue Access can allow some drivers to receive requests before others in the airport queue.

Uber’s airport technology blog explains why the app shows airport information differently from normal city areas. Uber says airport driver and supply signals include flight, weather and rider app activity, and driver queue signals are used because airport rules can require drivers to be staged in a waiting lot before dispatch.
## Rules to follow at the airport

Uber Help says drivers should pick up passengers only at authorised pickup areas and avoid blocking traffic lanes. It also says drivers should wait for dispatch only in the approved staging lot shown by the Driver app and airport signage.

This is important in Indian airports because each terminal can have its own pickup point. Delhi Airport says app-based cabs are available at T1 outside the arrivals zone, at T2 outside the arrivals zone, and at T3 in the Multi-Level Car Park on Level 0.

Mumbai Airport’s FAQ says app-based cabs such as Ola and Uber use Terminal 2 Arrival P4 and Terminal 1 Ground Transportation level for arrivals. The same FAQ lists separate Terminal 2 arrival points for some Uber categories, including P6 and P7.

Before you enter the airport road, check the app and the airport signs together. If the rider is not at the pickup point, Uber says you can call or text the rider from the Driver app, but the pickup should still happen at the approved location.
## How to decide if an airport run is worth it

The best time to wait for an airport trip back to the city is when you have already dropped a rider at the airport, according to Uber Help. That is because you are already there, so you are not spending extra time just to reach the queue.

Before going empty to the airport, check three things in the app and on the airport arrivals page. Check the expected wait, the number of cars already in queue if shown, and whether several flights are landing soon.

The Indian Express reported in March 2023 that Uber’s driver app update shows approximate airport waiting time, the number of cars in the airport Uber zone, and expected flight arrivals over the next hour. Use these signals before deciding to leave a busy city area for the airport.

A simple habit is to compare airport waiting time with the trips you could get nearby in the city. If the airport shows a long wait and there are fewer arrivals, staying in city zones may keep your wheels moving more often.

Also check your car before choosing the airport queue. If your CNG level, EV charge, FASTag balance or phone battery is low, finish those jobs before entering the airport system, because leaving the waiting area can push you out of the queue.
For late-night airport work, keep the pickup zone clear in your mind before the rider calls. A calm call saying the terminal, pickup level and bay shown in the app can save time for both of you.
Airport trips can be useful when you treat the queue as one option, not the whole plan. If you need a car for app-based driving, Everest Fleet is one place you can go for a car.

title: Uber Incentives for Drivers in India Weekly Quest Guide
excerpt: Learn where to find Uber driver incentives, how Quest and Boost+ work, and how to plan trips that count.
body: If you search for uber incentives for drivers in india, the main thing to know is simple. Uber shows eligible incentives inside the Driver app, and you should read each offer before planning your day around it.
## What Uber incentives mean in the Driver app

Uber’s own Help page says drivers may be offered different promotions at different times. The factors can include when or where you normally drive, how long you have been driving, and how many trips you have completed during the week.

This means two drivers in the same city may not see the same offer. It also means you may have a promotion one week and no promotion the next week. Uber Help says promotions change weekly, vary by city and driver, and are not guaranteed every week.

Do not plan your fuel, CNG fill, charging stop, or long shift only on what another driver tells you. Open your own Driver app and check your own Opportunities section. The offer shown in your app is the one that matters for you.

If you signed up in one city but are now driving in another, Uber Help says you may not receive promotions for the current city. It also says it can take up to 21 days to start receiving promotions in a new city. If this applies to you, contact Support through the app and ask to update your city.
## How Quest, Boost+, Flash Incentives and other offers work

A Quest is a trip-goal offer. Uber Help describes it as a promotion where you earn extra money after reaching certain trip goals within a set time. For a cab driver, the important words are trip goal and set time. If the offer ends before you finish the required trips, the remaining trips may not help you complete that Quest.

Uber Help also lists hourly guarantee, consecutive trips, and service fee quest as promotion types. In an hourly guarantee, Uber says the offer shows a minimum amount you take home if you drive for a full hour and complete the required number of trips. In a consecutive trips offer, you complete multiple trips in a row when and where Uber expects more riders. In a service fee quest, Uber sets a trip threshold and then offers a discounted service fee on the remaining trips during that quest period.

Boost+ works differently from a weekly Quest. Uber Help says Boost+ promotions are paid immediately after an eligible trip and appear on the trip receipt. So after a Boost+ trip, check the receipt instead of waiting only for the end of the week.

Flash Incentives are also shown trip by trip. Uber Help says they are not available on every request, not every driver will see them, and they can depend on the trip, city, and current area conditions. If a Flash Incentive is included, Uber says it is shown before you accept the trip. After the trip, you can check it in the payment breakdown by opening the Driver app, tapping Earnings, and selecting See details.
## Where to find your offers and progress

Uber Help gives the main path clearly. Open the Driver app, tap the menu icon at the top left, and select Opportunities. The pinned carousel shows active promotions and upcoming promotions. Tap an offer to see more details.

For Quest progress, Uber says to go to the menu and open Opportunities. Active quests and promotions appear there, and tapping them shows your progress toward the goal. Check this before you go online, during breaks, and before you stop for the day.

The Google Play listing for Uber Driver, updated on 28 September 2026, says drivers can find Quests, Boost+, and earning opportunities in the Discover tab. App screens can change by version and city, so check both Opportunities and Discover if you do not see an offer where you expected it.

Use the Earnings section to confirm what has already been paid. Uber Help says you can track earnings by week, day, or trip by tapping the fare icon at the top of the screen or through the Earnings tab. The same page says the Trip History tab shows recent trips, and selecting a trip shows the gross fare and net fare for that trip.
## How to plan your week so trips count

Start by reading the full promotion terms in your own app. Uber Help says each promotion has different eligibility requirements, so do not assume every trip, time, or area will count in the same way. If the offer says a set time, plan your shift inside that time. If it says a location or ride type in the app, keep your work inside those conditions.

Plan around completed trips, not only online hours. A Quest is about reaching trip goals in a set time, and an hourly guarantee also needs the required number of trips. Short breaks are useful, but long gaps during an active offer can make it harder to finish the target before the offer ends.

Use the app’s demand signals, but keep your route practical. Uber Help says the app can show upcoming events in Opportunities, airport trends on the home screen, and surge areas on the main map. These tools can help you choose where to wait, but you should still think about fuel, charging, CNG availability, parking rules, and how far you are from likely pickups.

At the end of each driving day, compare your promotion progress with your Earnings and Trip History. For Boost+ and Flash Incentives, check the trip receipt or payment breakdown soon after the ride. If you believe a promotion was paid incorrectly, Uber Help says you can report a promotion issue after selecting the promotion type in Help.

This is not a promise of extra income. Incentives change by week, city, driver, and trip request. The safest habit is to check your own app daily, read the offer before accepting long shifts, and confirm payment details after the trips are completed.

title: Uber Driver Acceptance Rate and Cancellation Rate Guide
excerpt: Learn where to check your Uber rates, how they affect trip flow and offers, and simple habits to reduce cancellations.
body: If you search for “uber driver acceptance rate and cancellation rate”, this guide explains the two numbers in simple words. These rates matter because Uber uses them to show your trip behaviour, and some promotions or Uber Pro rewards can depend on them.
## What the two rates mean
Acceptance rate is the share of ride requests you accept compared with the requests you receive. Uber Help says this rate is shown for the last 30 days, and it may update with a delay.

Cancellation rate is different. Uber India’s Community Guidelines say it is calculated as the percentage of trips cancelled out of your last 100 accepted requests. This includes trips you cancel, and in some cases rider cancellations that Uber says may be linked to your actions.
A simple way to remember it is this. If you are online and a request comes, accepting or declining affects acceptance rate. If you accept first and then cancel, it affects cancellation rate.

Uber says drivers with good quality typically have a cancellation rate below 5%. You do not need to panic about one genuine problem, but repeated cancellations can hurt your account quality and your access to some rewards.
## Where to see the numbers in the app

Uber Help says you can view your acceptance rate and cancellation rate in your Partner Area or by going to your Profile at the top right corner of the app. If the number looks old, Uber recommends restarting the app because the rate may update after a delay.

For promotions, check the correct screen. Uber Help says promotion-specific acceptance and cancellation rates are shown in the Earnings tab, not only in the Ratings tab. Open the Driver app, go to Earnings, tap Promotions, and then open the promotion to see its rules and your progress.

This matters because your overall rate and your promotion rate may not be the same. A promotion may count only a specific time, area or set of trips. Always read the offer in the app before you start chasing it.

Uber’s Driver app page also says the app shows your earnings after each trip and lets you track daily and weekly goals. Use that along with your rates, so you know whether your online time is turning into completed trips.
## How rates connect to trip flow and incentives

Uber says a high acceptance rate helps reduce waiting time for riders and pickup time for drivers. In daily work, that means you should go online only when you are ready to take a trip, reach the pickup, and complete the ride.

Promotions usually require completed trips. Uber Help says cancelled trips do not count for minimum completed trip requirements, and cancelled trips are excluded when trips per hour are calculated for a promotion.

Some promotions may also have acceptance rate rules, opt-in rules, online hour rules, or location rules. Uber says location-based trips are counted by the rider’s request pickup location, not by where you were standing when you accepted the trip.

Uber Pro can also use these numbers. Uber India’s Uber Pro terms say active eligible drivers in participating cities are automatically enrolled, and Gold, Platinum and Diamond tiers need points plus programme standards such as rating, cancellation rate and acceptance rate. The exact standards and calculation method are shown inside the Uber Driver app for your city.

The Uber Pro terms also say points are earned in fixed 3-month periods and reset at the end of each period. They add that cancellation and acceptance rates may take about 72 hours to refresh in the programme account.

For four-wheeler drivers, Uber Pro terms mention some city-specific rewards such as Pro Perk in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chandigarh. Do not assume a reward is active for you only because another driver has it. Check the Uber Pro screen in your own app and city.
## How to keep cancellations low

The best habit is to go online only when you are fully ready. Before tapping Go Online, finish tea, toilet breaks, CNG filling, charging, cash change, document checks and any personal call. If you need a break, log off instead of staying online and declining or cancelling requests.

Keep your phone charged and mounted where you can see the request clearly. Poor battery, weak data or a hidden phone can make you miss important trip details. If the app is slow, stop safely, restart it and then continue.

Read the request before accepting. Check pickup distance, route direction, expected time, payment information if shown, and any promotion condition you are trying to complete. Accept only when you are willing to go to the pickup and complete the ride as shown in the app.

After accepting, call or message only when needed, and keep it polite and short. Do not ask the rider to cancel. Uber’s guidelines say cancellations can include cases where a rider cancellation may be attributed to the driver’s actions.

Plan fuel, CNG or charging before peak hours. Many cancellations happen because the car is not ready after the driver accepts a good request. If the tank is low, log off, fill up, and come back online near a busy area.

Use a simple end-of-day check. Open your rate screens, look at any active promotion, and note why cancellations happened that day. If the reason was avoidable, fix the routine the next day. If you need a car to start or continue cab work, you can speak to Everest Fleet.

title: How to Increase Uber Driver Rating With Daily Trip Habits
excerpt: A simple guide to what riders rate, how Uber ratings work, and daily habits that can protect your score.
body: If you search for how to increase Uber driver rating, start with the small things riders feel in the first two minutes. A clean car, working AC, calm driving, a clear route, a polite pickup call, and help with luggage can make the trip feel safe and easy.

This guide is for cab drivers using Uber and other ride-hailing apps in Indian cities. It does not promise extra income, but it explains habits that can support better ratings, fewer complaints, and steadier daily work.
## How Uber says driver ratings work

Uber says drivers and riders can rate each other from 1 to 5 stars after each trip. The rating is based on the trip experience, and the app may ask for more feedback when someone gives less than 5 stars.

Your driver rating on Uber is the average of your last 500 rated trips, according to Uber’s driver page. If you have done fewer than 500 rated trips, the average is based on the rated trips you have completed so far.

This means one bad rating is not the full story, especially after you have completed many trips. Uber also says ratings linked to issues outside your control, such as traffic, app issues, or pricing, may be excluded from your score.

You can check your rating, feedback, and compliments in the Driver app. Uber says you can tap the menu icon, tap your profile photo, and then tap the average rating under your name to see the details.
## What riders usually notice first

The first thing many riders notice is the car. Uber’s 5-star trip tips say riders appreciate a car that is clean, well maintained, and scent-free. Before your first trip, remove wrappers, bottles, dust, and any strong smell from the cabin.

AC also matters in Indian city traffic. Uber’s India vehicle requirements page lists working windows and air conditioning for UberX and UberXL, so check the AC before going online, not after a rider complains.
Keep a small cloth in the car and wipe the dashboard, door handles, and rear seat area during breaks. If you drive a CNG car, also check the boot area so luggage space is clean and safe to use.
A rider may not remember your whole day of driving. They will remember whether the car felt ready for them when they opened the door.
## Pickup, route, and conversation habits

A polite pickup call can prevent confusion at a mall gate, society tower, station road, or office park. Keep the call short. Say your name, confirm the pickup point, and ask for a clear landmark if the pin is not exact.
Do not sound irritated if the rider takes a minute to explain the gate or lane. Uber’s Community Guidelines ask riders and drivers to treat each other with respect, and the same tone helps at pickup.
For the route, start with the app navigation, then ask if the rider has a preferred route. Uber’s 5-star trip tips say a rider’s preferred route may be different from what navigation shows.
If the rider suggests another road, confirm it calmly before changing. If you must change because of a closure, traffic, or a no-entry point, explain it in one sentence and continue driving safely.

Conversation should be light. Uber says many 5-star drivers greet riders at the start and then let the rider decide whether to talk. This is useful in morning office rides, airport rides, and late evening rides when many riders prefer a quiet trip.
## Safe driving and end-of-trip habits

Calm driving is one of the strongest rating habits because the rider feels every brake, turn, and lane change. Delhi Traffic Police safety guidelines say drivers should follow signals, avoid mobile phone distraction, keep a safe distance, follow speed limits, and regularly check brakes, tyres, lights, and signals.

Use a phone mount and do not scroll while moving. If you need to check the map closely, stop safely first. A rider may not say anything during the trip, but unsafe phone use can show up later in feedback.
At the drop point, stop where it is safe and allowed. If the rider has luggage, offer help when it is safe to step out. Uber’s rating guidance says riders appreciate help with doors and luggage.

Before ending your shift, read your weekly review if it is available in the app. Uber says this review shares ratings and rider comments, so treat it like a service report. If the same issue appears again, such as car smell, route choice, or harsh braking, fix that first the next day.

Good ratings come from repeatable habits, not one special trip. Keep the car clean, keep the AC working, speak calmly, drive smoothly, and make the rider feel that the trip is under control. If you need a car for cab work, you can also visit Everest Fleet.

title: Uber Driver Best Locations and Waiting Tips for More Trips
excerpt: Learn how to choose better waiting spots, cut empty kilometres, and use app signals before moving across the city.
body: If you search for “uber driver best locations”, the useful answer is not one fixed place. The better habit is to read demand in the app, know where riders gather in your city, and wait where the next pickup can reach you quickly.
## Start with the app, not only with guesswork

Uber says its Driver app has Hourly Trends under Earnings trends, where you can check busy times for your city. It also says the heat map uses lighter and darker colours to show demand levels, with darker areas showing higher demand or surge in places where surge applies.

Before you drive across the city, open the map and zoom out. If two busy areas are close, choose the one that is easier to enter and leave. A busy lane where you get stuck for twenty minutes can be worse than a slightly quieter road where pickups are faster.

Uber also says surge can change quickly because rates update with demand in real time. Treat a dark patch as a signal, not a guarantee. If it disappears while you are still far away, stop chasing it and look for the next practical pocket nearby.
## Know the places where requests usually gather

Airports, railway stations, office districts, tech parks, malls, hospitals, hotels, restaurants, and nightlife streets all work differently. Your job is to match the place with the time and the road layout, not just park at the gate.

For airports, Uber says some airports use a Virtual Queue where the first driver to enter the designated area is first in line for a request. Uber also says you must wait inside the marked waiting area shown in the Driver app, and staying outside it can stop you from receiving airport requests.

For railway stations and malls, look for the pickup point that riders can find without calling you many times. Uber’s New Delhi city page shows popular destinations such as Ambience Mall and Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station, and its city pages also group places under transport, hotels, entertainment, and restaurants. These are useful clues for the kind of areas where riders may open the app.

Office districts and tech parks are different because demand often follows shift times. Outlook Business reported that Uber is targeting employee transport to offices, IT parks, factories, and global capability centres because these commutes can be predictable and large in volume. For you, that means business parks may be useful at office start and closing times, while food streets and hotel areas may work better later in the evening.
## Cut empty kilometres after every drop

Empty kilometres are the silent cost in app driving. After each drop, do not immediately drive back to your favourite stand. First check the map near the drop location, then check if the rider’s destination area has offices, malls, hotels, hospitals, colleges, railway access, or a main road with legal stopping space.

Uber’s upfront fare page says trip details can include pickup location, dropoff location, estimated trip length, estimated trip duration, and traffic. It also says demand at the destination and the chance of getting another trip quickly can affect how offers are worked out. This is why a trip ending in a busy area can be more useful than a trip that leaves you far outside demand.

Use the Driver Destination feature when you are moving toward home, a CNG pump, a charging point, or your planned break area. Uber says you can set a destination and the app looks for riders going in the same general direction. It also says the feature can be used two times per day.

If you are between two demand areas, move slowly toward the nearer one instead of making a long empty run. Keep your phone charged, data on, GPS steady, and app online. A weak signal can make the app think you are not where you really are, especially around large buildings and airport zones.
## Choose waiting spots that reduce pickup time

The best waiting spot is not always the front gate. It is usually a legal, safe place near an exit road, service lane, parking area, or tea stall where you can start moving without blocking traffic. Avoid standing at hospital emergency gates, hotel porch areas, mall entry ramps, or station exits where guards may ask you to move.

At airports, follow the app’s marked waiting area and pickup rules. Uber says pickup areas can be blocked for new requests to avoid congestion and safety issues, so stopping at the departure gate is not the same as joining the queue. If the app shows an estimated airport wait time in your city, compare that time with the demand outside the airport before deciding to stay.

At malls, stations, hotels, and nightlife areas, wait where the rider can walk to the car easily and where your car can face the exit direction. If you are on the wrong side of a divider, the pickup may become a long U-turn. If the road has a no-stopping zone, move to the next legal side road and call only after accepting the trip if the pickup point is unclear.

A simple daily habit helps. Note three places where you got quick back-to-back trips, and note the time, road side, and waiting point. After a week, your own city map becomes more useful than any general tip. If you need a car for app-based driving, Everest Fleet is one place drivers can go for a car.

title: Best Time to Drive Uber on Weekdays and Weekends in India
excerpt: Learn how to plan weekday and weekend shifts around rush hours, evenings, rain, events and surge areas.
body: If you search for the best time to drive Uber on weekdays and weekends, the answer is simple but city-specific. Ride requests usually rise during office travel, evenings, weekends, bad weather and special events, so your shift should be planned around those windows, not only around the clock.
## Start with your city’s busy hours

Uber Help says busy times usually include weekends, morning and evening rush hours, and evening hours. That matches the daily pattern you see in most Indian cities, where people travel to offices, colleges, stations, markets, restaurants and homes at fixed times.

Use the Driver app before you start. Uber Help says you can open the app, tap the arrow icon in the lower-left corner, choose “See hourly trends”, and select the city or area shown next to “View For”. This chart is useful because one part of the city can be busy while another part is slow.

For weekdays, think of your day in blocks. The morning block is for office, school and station trips. The evening block is for office returns, shopping, dinner and late trains or flights. If you drive the full day, keep your longest break in a slower middle period instead of leaving the road during peak demand.
## Plan around office and school movement

A government travel survey gives a clear reason why mornings matter. The Press Information Bureau said on October 5, 2026 that the National Statistics Office survey covered July 2025 to June 2026 and found that 94.9 percent of workers going to fixed workplaces leave before 10:00 AM. The same release said worker departures peak from 8:00 AM to 10:00 AM, with 56.5 percent leaving in that window.

The same survey said 82.0 percent of students depart between 7:00 AM and 10:00 AM, with the biggest school departure window from 8:00 AM to 9:00 AM. For a cab driver, this means early morning demand can build around residential areas, metro stations, railway stations, bus stands, schools, colleges and office roads.

Do not look only at demand. Look at traffic and pickup time too. Uber India’s Upfront Fares page says real-time demand can include surge pricing, how busy the pickup area is, how busy the destination is, the chance of getting another trip quickly, and traffic. A trip that takes you to another busy area can be better for your next ride than a trip that leaves you far from demand.
## Use weekends, evenings and late nights carefully

Uber India’s 2025 travel report, as reported by ETTravelWorld, found that 6:00 PM was the most common booking time and Friday was the busiest day for ride requests in 2025. The same report said Mumbai and Kolkata led in late-night trips, while Bhubaneswar and Thiruvananthapuram had the highest share of office-hour rides.

This tells you not to copy another city blindly. In an office-heavy city or area, weekday morning and evening trips may matter most. In a city with strong nightlife, railway movement, airport movement or weekend shopping, Friday evening, Saturday evening and Sunday return trips can be stronger.

Festival and wedding nights should be treated like special-event nights. Uber’s surge page says special events can bring many riders to the app at the same time. On such nights, check the heat map before you move, keep enough fuel or charge, and avoid driving empty for a long distance only because you heard one area is busy.
## Read surge, but do not chase it blindly

Uber says surge pricing happens when ride demand is high and there are not enough cars nearby. The app may show a multiplier, an additional surge amount, or an upfront fare that includes surge, depending on the city. Uber also says surge updates in real time and can be specific to one neighbourhood.

In the Driver app, shaded areas show demand. Uber Help says darker shades show higher demand, while brighter or lighter areas show lower demand. It also says you may see surge labels such as 1.3x, 1.4x or 2.1x when you zoom in, but the latest amount should be checked at the bottom of the screen.

A simple rule is to move towards nearby demand, not faraway demand. If a red area is close, it may be worth going there. If it is far and traffic is heavy, the surge may reduce before you arrive. Watch whether the area is near offices, malls, stations, airports, hotels or event venues, because these places can produce more than one trip.
## Build a shift that keeps you near demand

Before going online, check hourly trends and decide your first pickup area. During the shift, use the heat map and your trip offer details together. Uber India says upfront trip information can show how much you will make including surge pricing, where you will go, pickup time and distance, and drop-off time and distance.

For weekdays, one practical plan is to start near homes or transport points before the morning rush, move towards office districts during the day, take a break after the rush, and return before the evening office exit. For weekends, start later if your city wakes up late, but be ready for evening shopping, restaurant, station, airport and family travel.

For rain, first keep safety above demand. Uber says bad weather can cause many people to request rides at the same time. If roads are waterlogged or visibility is poor, slow down, keep extra distance, and choose pickups where you can stop safely without blocking traffic.

The best shift is not the longest shift. It is the shift where more of your online time is close to real demand, with fewer empty kilometres and fewer long waits. If you need a car for app-based driving, Everest Fleet is one place where drivers can go for a car.

title: FASTag Local Pass Rules for Drivers Near Toll Plazas
excerpt: Learn who can use the new annual FASTag local pass, what it costs, and what cab drivers should check before applying.
body: A new concessional FASTag local pass starts at eligible National Highway fee plazas from November 1, 2026. It is useful for people who live near one toll plaza, but cab drivers must note one important point: MoRTH says it is only for non-commercial vehicles with a valid and functional FASTag.
## What the new local pass is

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, through PIB, said the Government of India has introduced a Concessional Local Pass for eligible non-commercial vehicle owners who live within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza. The rule comes into effect on November 1, 2026.

This pass is for travel through one specific fee plaza. PIB said it will be valid only for that fee plaza and will not be transferable to any other plaza. This means it is not a pass for all toll plazas on a route.

The annual fee is based on the location of the fee plaza. According to PIB, the pass will cost Rs 1,500 per year where the fee plaza is outside a municipal or local town area, and Rs 3,000 per year where the fee plaza is within those limits.

PIB also said the rates may be revised every year by the Central Government, with any revision taking effect on April 1. So if you are planning for yearly running cost, check the current fee before paying.
## Who it applies to, and who should be careful
The pass is for eligible non-commercial vehicle owners. PIB said the vehicle must have a valid and functional FASTag, and the owner must live within 20 km of the fee plaza.

For cab drivers, the most important check is the vehicle category. If your car is registered for commercial use as a taxi or cab, this local pass is not meant for that vehicle because the official release says it is for non-commercial vehicles.

This may still matter to you if you own a private car at home and live near a National Highway fee plaza. It may also matter to car owners who are not using the car as a taxi and regularly cross the same nearby plaza.

The local pass is different from the general FASTag annual pass. Autocar India reported that the standard FASTag annual pass costs Rs 3,075 for 2026-27, while this new local pass costs Rs 1,500 or Rs 3,000 depending on the plaza location. The local pass is cheaper in some cases, but it works only at the selected fee plaza.
## When and where you can get it
PIB said the Annual Local Pass will be available at eligible toll plazas from November 1, 2026. The same release said it will also be available through the Rajmargyatra App from December 1, 2026.

This date difference is important. If you want to apply during November 2026, check at the eligible toll plaza first. If you prefer the app route, wait for the Rajmargyatra App option from December 1, 2026, as stated by PIB.

The Indian Express reported that the eligible toll plaza list will become available on the Rajmargyatra app. The same report said the facility is integrated with DigiLocker and VAHAN to retrieve the commuter’s address, vehicle details and linked FASTag for checking the 20 km condition.

Before applying, make sure your FASTag is active and working. Also check that your vehicle details in VAHAN and your address details used for verification are correct, because the 20 km rule depends on residence near the fee plaza.
## Where the pass will not work
The pass will not be available everywhere. PIB said it will not be issued on National Highways or Expressways where toll fee collection is based on a closed user-fee collection system.
PIB also said the pass will not be issued where a service road or alternative road is available for use by commuters. So living within 20 km does not by itself confirm that you will get the pass.

Business Standard reported that eligible vehicle owners can choose between the existing monthly pass and the new annual local pass. This means you should compare your present monthly cost with the annual cost before deciding.

If you cross many toll plazas for airport trips, outstation trips or intercity duty, this local pass may not help for those other plazas. It is made for regular movement through one nearby fee plaza, not for full-route toll savings.
## What you should check before paying
First, check whether your vehicle is non-commercial or commercial. If it is a cab with commercial registration, do not assume this pass will apply to your working car.
Next, check the fee plaza. Confirm whether it is covered, whether it is outside or inside municipal or local town limits, and whether the yearly fee is Rs 1,500 or Rs 3,000.

Then check your actual use. If you cross the same eligible plaza often in a private vehicle, the local pass may be useful. If your driving is mainly on different routes and different toll plazas, normal FASTag deductions or another applicable pass may be more relevant.

Keep your FASTag balance active even if you use a pass, because the pass is linked to a valid and functional FASTag. Also remember that once the pass is tied to one fee plaza, it cannot be shifted to another plaza for your convenience.

title: e-Shram Card Guide for Cab and Platform Drivers
excerpt: Learn who can register on e-Shram, what to keep ready, and how the UAN card can help you track welfare schemes.
body: The Labour Ministry’s Shram Samvad programme in Lucknow on 26 and 27 October 2026 again put focus on social protection for unorganised, gig and platform workers. If you drive a cab on an app or work as an independent driver, this is a good time to check whether e-Shram registration is useful for you.
## What e-Shram is and why drivers should know it

e-Shram is the Government of India’s national database for unorganised workers, run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. After registration, a worker gets a 12-digit Universal Account Number, called UAN, and an e-Shram card.

The ministry says e-Shram is meant to help deliver welfare schemes and social security benefits to unorganised workers. It is also part of e-Shram One-Stop Solution, which brings many schemes into one place so a worker does not have to visit many different portals for every scheme.

For a driver, the important point is simple. The card does not by itself promise a fixed payment or job benefit, but it gives you an identity on the e-Shram system and helps you see schemes for which you may be able to apply.

The official e-Shram FAQ says the One-Stop Solution shows scheme categories such as health, insurance, pension, credit, housing, food security, employment and skilling. It also lists schemes including One Nation One Ration Card, PM-SYM, National Career Service, PMJJBY, PMSBY and Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY among schemes available on the platform.
## Who can register and what you need

The e-Shram FAQ says an unorganised worker is a home-based worker, self-employed worker or wage worker in the unorganised sector who is not a member of ESIC or EPFO. Many app-based and independent drivers may fit this broad idea, but you should check your own EPFO or ESIC status before registering.

Any person doing unorganised work and aged 16 years or above can register, subject to other conditions. The FAQ also says there is no income criterion for registering on e-Shram and no educational qualification is prescribed.

You need your Aadhaar number and an Aadhaar-linked mobile number for self-registration. If your mobile number is not linked to Aadhaar, the FAQ says you may visit the nearest Common Service Centre or State Seva Kendra and register through biometric authentication.

Registration is free. The official FAQ clearly says workers are not required to pay any charge to any registering entity. If you go through a CSC, carry your Aadhaar number and mobile, as the FAQ says no other document has to be submitted at the centre.
## How to register or update your card
You can access e-Shram services through the official e-Shram portal. The FAQ says workers may register themselves on the portal or use an assisted route by visiting the nearest CSC.
Before starting, keep your Aadhaar, mobile phone and bank details ready. Use your own phone number if possible, because OTPs and future updates are easier when the number is in your control.

While registering, choose the occupation that matches your current work. The FAQ says the worker must select the occupation that best represents the activity currently being done. If driving is your main source of income, choose the closest driving-related occupation shown on the portal.

If you are already registered, you do not need to register again for e-Shram One-Stop Solution. The FAQ says existing registrants can use their UAN to log in and monitor schemes in which they are enrolled.

Keep your details updated. The e-Shram homepage advises registrants to update their profile and occupation for continued benefits. The FAQ says you can update address, contact number, bank account information and other details by logging in with UAN and OTP, or through a CSC.
## What to check after registration

After login, the e-Shram FAQ says the homepage can show your name and UAN, profile picture, update profile tabs, download UAN card option, find eligible schemes option, looking for a job option, scheme enrolment categories and enrolled schemes.

Check the Find Eligible Schemes section when you have time, not during duty hours. If the portal shows an Apply button for a scheme, the FAQ says it means you are not yet enrolled and can start enrolment. If it shows View, it means you are already enrolled and can check details.

The e-Shram card does not expire, and the FAQ says renewal is not required. Still, you should update your mobile number, address, bank account and occupation whenever they change, because wrong details can create problems when you try to use a scheme.

For help, the e-Shram site shows helpdesk numbers 14434 and 18008896811, with timing from 9.00 AM to 6.00 PM daily, including Sundays. If you are registering through a CSC, ask the operator to let you check the details before final submission, especially your name, mobile number, occupation and bank details.
Do not share OTPs with unknown people and do not pay for e-Shram registration. If you need a car to drive on platforms, Everest Fleet is one place where drivers can enquire for a car.

title: Hyundai Bayon CNG Guide for Cab Drivers Before Booking
excerpt: Cab drivers can check the Bayon petrol details now and wait for confirmed CNG figures before booking.
body: Hyundai launched the Bayon in India on October 26, 2026, and its CNG version is planned for January 2027. If you drive on Uber, Ola, Rapido or another app, the useful point is simple: the petrol car is available now, but the CNG facts that matter for daily earnings still need to be checked at launch.
## What has changed now

According to Hyundai Motor India, the Bayon has been launched at a starting price of Rs 9,99,900, ex-showroom. The company has started with a four-cylinder 1.5-litre MPi petrol engine. Hyundai says this engine makes 84.4 kW, or 115 PS, and 143.8 Nm of torque.

Hyundai says the petrol Bayon comes with a 6-speed manual transmission or an Intelligent Variable Transmission. For a cab driver, this means there are manual and automatic petrol options to compare today. The CNG option is not on sale yet, so do not calculate running cost using guessed mileage or guessed CNG pricing.

Autocar India reported on October 26, 2026 that Hyundai has confirmed a Bayon CNG launch in January 2027. CarWale also reported the January 2027 timing and said the petrol range starts at Rs 10 lakh. Treat January 2027 as the month to recheck the actual CNG price, variants, warranty, tank layout and mileage figure.
## Who should wait for the CNG version

If your trips are mostly inside a city, CNG may be the version to watch. Many cab drivers prefer CNG because the fuel cost can be easier to control when CNG pumps are available on their route. The Bayon CNG details are still not complete, so waiting can stop you from booking the wrong version too early.

If you drive long airport trips, late-night trips or intercity trips, first check CNG pump access near your regular stands. A CNG car can save money only when refuelling does not waste too much working time. Before booking, note the CNG stations you actually use in the morning, evening and after midnight.

If you carry luggage often, do not assume the CNG version will have the same usable boot as the petrol car. Hyundai says the petrol Bayon has 505 litres of boot space. When the CNG car reaches showrooms, open the boot yourself, place one large suitcase or airport bag inside, and check whether your normal passenger luggage still fits.
## Petrol Bayon details to check for cab use

Hyundai says the Bayon has a 2,600 mm wheelbase. The company also says it has rear AC vents, two-step rear reclining seats, 60:40 split rear seats and C-type USB charging ports. These are useful details to check because passengers notice rear-seat comfort, cooling and phone charging during longer rides.

Hyundai says more than 35 safety features are standard across all variants. The company names six airbags, Electronic Stability Control, Hill-start Assist Control, Roll Over Sensor and Tyre Pressure Monitoring System as standard features. If you are comparing variants, ask the dealer to show the exact feature list for the variant you are considering, not just the top model brochure.

The official press note also says the Bayon has more than 80 advanced safety features, including Hyundai SmartSense Level 2 Pro ADAS with 23 driver assistance features. For cab work, ask how these systems behave in dense city traffic and whether they can be adjusted through the car settings. Take a test drive in the kind of road conditions where you normally work.
## What to ask before booking in January

When the CNG version is shown in January 2027, ask for the official price sheet first. Compare the CNG variant with the petrol variant that has the same comfort and safety features. Do not compare a higher CNG variant with a lower petrol variant, because that can make the cost difference look wrong.

Ask the showroom for the official mileage or certified fuel efficiency figure when it is released. Also ask for the CNG tank capacity, tank position, spare wheel position, boot space after the tank fitment and the service schedule. These points affect your daily trips more than touchscreens or music systems.

Ask clearly whether the variant can be registered for commercial use in your city. Also ask what documents the dealer will provide for CNG endorsement, warranty and insurance. If you plan to attach the car to an app platform, check the platform’s accepted vehicle age, fuel type, seating and document rules before paying a booking amount.

Do a cost check on paper before deciding. Write your average kilometres per day, your city’s CNG price, your likely mileage, service cost and loan or monthly cost. Use confirmed numbers only after Hyundai announces the CNG variant details, because guessed numbers can make a car look cheaper than it really is.

title: PM E-DRIVE EV Charging Support Guide for Cab Drivers
excerpt: Learn what PM E-DRIVE means for EV charging, e-vouchers and vehicle checks before you shift to electric work.
body: PM E-DRIVE is the Central Government scheme for electric vehicles and charging infrastructure. For cab drivers, the main point is simple: it may improve public charging access, but you should check vehicle eligibility carefully before buying or renting an EV for work.
## What PM E-DRIVE covers

PM E-DRIVE stands for PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement. The Ministry of Heavy Industries says the scheme was launched through a Gazette notification dated 29 September 2024 and implemented from October 2024.

The latest PIB factsheet opened for this post says the scheme has been extended until 31 March 2028. It gives the total outlay as ₹11,900 crore and says the scheme supports demand incentives and infrastructure support across different EV categories.

The categories listed by PIB are registered electric two-wheelers, electric three-wheelers, e-ambulances, e-trucks, e-buses, charging infrastructure and upgradation of testing agencies. Electric taxi cars are not listed as a demand-incentive category on the official pages opened for this post, so do not assume that a cab car will get a PM E-DRIVE purchase benefit.

This matters if you are planning to move from CNG or diesel to an EV. The scheme may help the wider charging network, but your car choice, charging time and daily route still decide whether EV work is practical for you.
## Charging support that can help daily work

PIB says ₹2,000 crore has been earmarked for nationwide EV public charging stations under PM E-DRIVE. The same PIB factsheet says ₹851 crore had been approved for deployment of 8,147 chargers to three oil marketing companies and 10 states as of 28 September 2026.

Another PIB release explains where supported charging stations can come up. It lists places such as railway stations, airports operated and maintained by the Airports Authority of India, public sector oil company retail outlets, state transport bus stations, metro stations, municipal parking lots, public sector ports, toll plazas controlled by NHAI or state governments, and way-side amenities on highways and expressways.

For a driver, these locations are useful because they are close to real trip points. Airport queues, station pickups, highway rides and city parking breaks are places where a planned charge can save time. Before depending on any new charger, check whether it is working, what plug type it has, what the tariff is and whether parking is allowed while charging.

The official release also says government departments, central public sector enterprises, states, Union Territories and their public sector undertakings are eligible to submit proposals for EV public charging stations. This means a driver does not apply directly for a public charger under this scheme. You benefit when the charger becomes available for public use.
## E-vouchers and buyer checks

The PM E-DRIVE portal says the Ministry of Heavy Industries uses e-vouchers for eligible EV customers to get the demand incentive. The portal says the e-voucher is generated at the time of purchase after Aadhaar Face authentication, and a download link is sent to the customer’s registered mobile number.

The FAQ page says only one EV of a specific category per individual will qualify for incentives. It also says individuals must validate Aadhaar authentication linked to their mobile number, and each mobile number can be used only once for incentive purposes.

The FAQ page also says resold EVs are not eligible for incentives, and only the original purchase qualifies. It says EVs manufactured under the FAME-II scheme are not eligible for incentives under PM E-DRIVE 2024.

If you are buying an eligible EV, ask the dealer to show the model’s eligibility on the PM E-DRIVE portal before you make the final payment. Keep your Aadhaar-linked mobile number active, check the invoice, and confirm that the incentive has been adjusted in the vehicle price if the model is eligible.
## What cab drivers should do before shifting to EV

First, separate two questions. One is whether the vehicle gets a government incentive. The other is whether the vehicle can earn well on your route after charging time, parking time and daily kilometres are counted.

If you work long airport or highway trips, check charging points on both ends of the route, not only near your home. If you work inside the city, check whether there is a charger near your usual waiting area, lunch stop or night parking location.

If you rent or take a car on a monthly plan, ask who pays for charging, where the car can be charged and what happens if a charger is down. Ask about battery range with AC on, charging time from low battery to usable range, and whether the car supports fast charging.

Keep your driving licence, registration certificate, insurance, permit, PUC and fitness-related documents ready as usual. EVs reduce fuel-station visits, but they do not reduce your duty to carry valid vehicle and driver documents on every trip.

PM E-DRIVE is useful to track because it shows where public charging support is going. For now, use it as one input in your EV decision, along with your city, duty hours, charging access and vehicle cost. If you want to drive a cab without owning a car, Everest Fleet is one place where you can ask for a car.

title: Proposed AEB and ADAS Rules for Taxi Drivers
excerpt: Understand the draft safety rules, key dates, and what to check before buying or running a taxi.
body: The Road Ministry has proposed new safety rules for passenger cars, including taxi cars, with dates from 2027 to 2032. These rules are still in draft form, so your present car does not need any change today.
## What the draft rule is about

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has published draft changes to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. Gazette Tracker’s text of the draft says the notification is G.S.R. 904(E), dated October 19, 2026, with issue date October 21, 2026 and publication date October 22, 2026.

The main feature is Advanced Emergency Braking System, or AEBS. Akashvani News explains that AEBS can apply the brakes if the driver does not respond in an emergency, either to avoid a crash or reduce the impact.

This is part of ADAS, which means advanced driver assistance systems. CarDekho explains that AEBS uses a camera, radar, or both to watch the road ahead, warn the driver, and then brake if there is no response.

The draft also covers steering effort, automatic steering functions, emergency lane keeping, driver drowsiness and attention warning, ISOFIX child-seat anchorage standards, and luggage retention requirements. These are not all starting on the same day, so drivers and owners should look at the date that applies to their vehicle type.
## Key dates for taxis and passenger cars

Autocar India states that M1 category vehicles are passenger vehicles with up to eight seats besides the driver. Most app-based taxi cars used for city rides will normally fall in this broad passenger-car category, but you should still confirm the vehicle category on the registration certificate or with the dealer when buying a new car.

From October 1, 2027, the Gazette text says steering effort on most motor vehicles manufactured on and after that date must meet AIS-193. It also says M1 vehicles with Automatic Command Steering Functionalities from that date must meet AIS-193, and M1 vehicles with Emergency Lane Keeping System from that date must meet AIS-191 Part 1.

The taxi-related date is October 1, 2029. The Gazette text says M1 vehicles to be registered as transport vehicles and manufactured on or after that date must be fitted with Automatic Command Steering Functionalities and Emergency Lane Keeping System. It also says such transport vehicles must have Driver Drowsiness and Attention Warning Systems meeting AIS-184.

For AEBS, there are two later dates. The Gazette text says M1 and N1 vehicles manufactured on and after October 1, 2028 must meet AIS-185 if they are provided with AEBS. It then says M1 vehicles manufactured on and after October 1, 2030 for new models, and October 1, 2032 for all models, must be fitted with AEBS meeting AIS-185.
## What it means if you drive today

There is no immediate change for a driver using an existing petrol, diesel, CNG, hybrid, or electric cab today. CarDekho says the draft does not ask existing owners to retrofit AEBS, and the proposal is not final yet.

If you are planning to buy a car now, you do not have to wait only because of this draft. But if you plan to keep the car for many years as a taxi, ask the dealer whether the car is an M1 vehicle, whether it is meant for private or transport registration, and whether any ADAS features already fitted meet the named AIS standards.

If you buy a car with AEBS or other ADAS features, take time to understand them before using the car for paid trips. CarDekho explains that under India’s AEBS standard, the system must warn the driver in at least two ways, such as sound, vibration, or visual alert, before braking.

CarDekho also says the driver can override AEBS by steering or pressing the accelerator, and the system cannot be switched off above 10 kmph. If it is switched off, it comes back on when the car is restarted. This matters in daily taxi work because different drivers may share the same car.
## Steps drivers and owners can take

First, remember that this is a draft rule. Gazette Tracker’s text says objections and suggestions will be considered within thirty days of the notification being published in the Gazette of India. CarDekho says comments can be emailed to comments-morth@gov.in before the window closes.

Second, keep the vehicle papers clear. When you buy or renew documents for a taxi, check whether the registration category says transport vehicle and whether the vehicle is in the M1 category. The proposed 2029 requirements are written for M1 vehicles to be registered as transport vehicles.

Third, ask for a simple feature explanation at delivery. If the car has lane keeping, automatic steering support, drowsiness warning, or AEBS, ask the showroom to show where the warning appears, what sound it makes, and how the driver can safely take control. This is useful when a car is driven by more than one person.

Fourth, keep your normal safe-driving habits. AEBS and driver warnings are support systems, not a replacement for watching the road, keeping distance, and resting when tired. The draft rule is about new vehicle standards, but your day-to-day driving still depends on attention and smooth control.
If you need a car for app-based work, Everest Fleet is one place where drivers can go for a car.

title: How Cab Drivers Can Use Tata EV’s 1,000 Charging Points
excerpt: EV cab drivers can learn where the new fast chargers matter and what to check before city or highway trips.
body: On 22 October 2026, TATA.ev’s MegaCharging network crossed 1,000 live charging connectors across India, according to Fortune India. For an EV cab driver, this mainly means more places to plan a fast top-up during city duty, airport trips, and intercity rides.
## What has changed for EV drivers

TATA.ev, the electric vehicle brand of Tata Motors, now has more than 1,000 live connectors under its MegaCharging network. Fortune India reported that the network covers 200 cities and 180 highway corridors, with 40 MW of installed charging capacity.

The company said the network has already powered 32 million electric kilometres. Fortune India also reported that it stretches from Amritsar in the north to Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu in the south, and from Dwarka in Gujarat to Murakati in Jharkhand in the east.

This is useful for drivers because charging options on known corridors reduce the chance of losing duty time while searching for a working charger. It is still important to check the charger status before you drive to the location, because every charger can have different availability, speed, and waiting time.
## Who can use these chargers
TATA.ev’s February 2025 press release said the Mega Charger network would be open to all EVs. It also said TATA.ev customers would get priority access and tariff benefits at these chargers.
This means you should not assume the charger is only for one car brand. If your EV supports the connector and the charging app shows the charger as available, you can plan a stop there.

TATA.ev had said it was working with charge point operators including Tata Power, ChargeZone, Statiq and Zeon. The same press release said partner chargers could be tracked and paid for through the iRA.ev app for TATA.ev users, instead of downloading many charging apps.

For a driver, the simple rule is to keep the correct charging apps ready before the trip starts. Do not wait until the battery is low to install an app, complete login, add payment, or check whether the charger is visible.
## Corridors and city spots that matter for cab work

Some MegaCharging sites are useful for city and airport duties. Tata Power said in September 2026 that the Tata Power x TATA.ev hub near Terminal 2 of Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport has 16 charging guns and 600 kW capacity, and is designed for private EV owners, taxis, ride-hailing fleets, and other frequent users.

Tata Power also listed hubs on the Yamuna Expressway between Greater Noida and Agra. It listed three locations on the Hyderabad to Vijayawada corridor, one on the Bengaluru to Tirupati route, one on the Pune to Bengaluru corridor, and city mobility hubs in Mumbai and Hyderabad.

The first 10 TATA.ev MegaChargers announced in May 2025 were placed on routes including Mumbai to Ahmedabad, Delhi to Jaipur, Pune to Nashik, Bengaluru city, and Udaipur city. The May 2025 TATA.ev release said these sites were chosen for highways and urban hubs, and mentioned facilities such as restrooms and dining at some locations.
If you drive airport trips or outstation rides, save two charging options on the route before you start. Keep one main stop and one backup stop, because a charger may be occupied when you reach.
## What to check before you start charging

Open the charging app and check whether the charger is live, what power rating it shows, and whether your car can use that charger. Tata Power says its EZ Charge app lets users see charging stations in real time, find a charger, and pay online.

Charging time is not the same for every car or every charger. Tata Power says public charging can take from 30 minutes to a few hours, depending on the charger’s power rating and the vehicle battery capacity.
Do not plan your duty assuming the fastest time every day. If your car battery is hot, the charger is shared, or your car cannot accept the full charger speed, your session may take longer.

Before plugging in, check the parking space, charging gun condition, app payment balance, and whether you need to move the car after charging. After the session starts, stay near the vehicle or keep checking the app, because a stopped session can waste valuable duty time.
## How drivers can use this in daily planning

For city work, use fast charging during natural breaks such as lunch, airport waiting time, or the gap after a long trip. For highway work, start with enough charge to reach the planned charger with a safe buffer, instead of reaching with a very low battery.

If you drive for an app, remember that the next ride may take you away from your preferred charger. It is safer to top up when you have a good charger nearby, rather than waiting for the battery to fall too low during peak hours.

Keep your charging bills and app records in case you track running cost for your vehicle. Also keep a simple note of reliable chargers on your regular routes, including which ones have toilets, food, shade, or less waiting time.
More charging points do not remove the need for planning, but they can make EV cab work easier when used well. If you want a car for cab work instead of buying one, you can also visit Everest Fleet.

title: Driving licence address change draft rules for drivers
excerpt: Learn what the proposed driving licence changes mean for address updates, documents, fees and learner licence tests.
body: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has proposed changes to driving licence rules that may make address and contact-detail updates simpler. These are draft rules, not final rules, so you should keep following the current process until the final notification is issued.
## What has been proposed

The draft amendment to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 was published in the Gazette on 21 October 2026, according to The Economic Times. It covers driving licence details, learner licence testing, documents, online applications and some fees.

For drivers, the most useful part is the proposed Rule 16A. The Gazette text carried by Gazette Tracker says an application to change particulars in a driving licence would be made on the portal in Form 2A, with valid proof for the correct details.

The same draft says the licensing authority would have 15 days to approve or reject a change in licence particulars. If it rejects the application, the reason must be recorded in writing and communicated to the applicant, including through electronic means.

For address change only, the draft adds one more protection. If the application is not accepted or rejected within 30 days, it would be treated as approved, according to the Gazette text carried by Gazette Tracker and NDTV Profit.
## Who should pay attention

This matters to you if your driving licence still shows an old address, old mobile number, old email ID or incorrect personal details. A cab driver often needs a clean and updated licence record for platform onboarding, vehicle paperwork, insurance work and RTO checks.

It also matters if you are planning to become a driver and have not yet received a learner licence. The Economic Times reported that the draft proposes raising the safe-driving tutorial pass mark from 60 percent to 75 percent, and the tutorial would have to be at least 30 minutes.

The draft does not mean your present licence becomes invalid. It also does not mean every RTO counter process has changed today. The Economic Times clearly says the proposals will take effect only after the government issues a final notification, and until then existing rules and fees continue to apply.

The Ministry has invited objections and suggestions within 30 days from the date the Gazette copies are made available to the public, according to the draft text. If you run a driving school, own cabs or handle driver documents, this is the period to read the draft carefully.
## Fees and documents to keep ready

The draft proposes that no fee should be charged for changing the address in a driving licence or updating the mobile number or email ID, according to the Gazette text carried by Gazette Tracker. NDTV Profit also reported that the proposed fee waiver would cover address, mobile number and email ID updates.

The draft also proposes no fee for certain services availed through online Aadhaar authentication. The Economic Times cautioned that the exact scope of fee exemptions will depend on the final notification, so do not assume that every licence service is free until the final rule is issued.

For address proof, the draft lists documents such as Aadhaar, voter photo identity card, passport, e-ration card, service photo identity card, pensioner photo identity card, electricity bill not older than three months, household gas bill not older than three months, and any other document prescribed by the state government. For foreign nationals, the draft also mentions proof of legal presence in India along with proof of residence.

For identity proof, the draft lists Aadhaar, valid Indian passport, e-ration card, service photo identity card, pensioner photo identity card and PAN. For age proof, it lists passport, recognised education certificate with date of birth, birth certificate, service photo identity card, pensioner photo identity card and other state-prescribed documents.

Before you apply, keep your current driving licence number, date of birth, mobile number, Aadhaar if you use Aadhaar authentication, and a clear address proof ready. If your electricity bill or gas bill is used, check the date because the draft mentions bills not older than three months.
## What you can do now

If your licence address is wrong, first check the existing online route instead of waiting for the draft to become final. The Uttarakhand Transport Department says licence-related services such as new learning licence, driving licence, renewal, change of address, change of mobile number and international driving permit can be availed online on the Sarathi portal, and that applicants can apply online 24x7.

Open the Sarathi portal from your state transport website or Parivahan, select your state, and choose the driving licence service for the work you need. If your state asks for an appointment or original documents at the RTO, follow that instruction because state-wise customisation can differ.

After applying, save the application number, payment receipt if any, uploaded document details and acknowledgement on your phone. Take screenshots also, because these are useful when you check status later or visit an RTO helpdesk.

If you are applying for a learner licence, prepare for a stricter tutorial test if the draft becomes final. Read road signs, lane rules, speed rules, parking rules and basic safety questions properly instead of rushing through the video or tutorial.

If you drive daily for work, make one folder on your phone for licence, RC, permit, insurance, PUC, fitness certificate if applicable, and challan receipts. A clean document folder saves time during onboarding, airport entry checks, toll issues and RTO visits.
If you need a car to start or continue cab driving, Everest Fleet is one place where drivers can go for a car.
